subject: Orion Commerce — Post-demo shortlist and ops asks
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie@orioncommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orion Commerce — Post-demo shortlist and ops asks

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the model shortlist we recommend for the POC, plus the immediate asks to make the 48-hour eval clean and measurable.

What we heard as priorities
- Latency target: sub-120ms avg for 512-token outputs in your low-latency checkout flow.
- Quality target: factual accuracy / low hallucination for product descriptions and spec extraction.
- Cost sensitivity: you want a clear per-1k-token estimate to compare against current vendor spend.

Shortlist (recommended for evaluation) — tradeoffs at a glance
1) RW-2.7B-optim (low-cost, low-latency)
   - Quality: good on template generation, weaker on long-context coherence and extraction recall
   - Median latency (our bench): ~45ms/token at 1k concurrency equivalent
   - Cost: ~0.8x baseline (best for high throughput conversational bursts)
2) RW-13B-quant (balanced accuracy/cost)
   - Quality: strong for extraction and mid-length description generation; better hallucination resistance
   - Median latency: ~95ms/token
   - Cost: ~2.6x baseline (recommended default for mixed workloads)
3) RW-70B-quant (highest quality, falling back to when accuracy is critical)
   - Quality: top-tier for nuance, entity recall, and long context; best for critical catalog curation
   - Median latency: ~210ms/token (without special batching/shortening)
   - Cost: ~7x baseline (use for a small % of traffic or as on-fallback)

Recommended evaluation plan
- Run a two-day (48h) A/B eval comparing RW-13B-quant and RW-70B-quant with your standard prompt set (attached: orion_prompt_pack_v1.json). If you want a cheaper baseline, include RW-2.7B-optim as a third arm.
- Benchmarks we’ll capture: avg latency @ 95th pct load, token accuracy (entity recall precision), generation ROUGE/F1 vs your reference prompts, and cost-per-1k tokens.
- Deliverables: per-model dashboard (link below), a prompt-level regression matrix, and a small sample of human-eval labels for high-risk prompts.

Immediate asks for you
- Confirm the acceptance criteria for the POC (latency & accuracy thresholds).
- Share the final 50 prompt samples you want prioritized during the run (we shipped a starter pack attached).
- Approve the 48-hour window to start as early as Tue 8/3 so we can get initial numbers back by Thu.

Links & attachments
- Benchmarks dashboard (internal): https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/orion-2027-07#summary
- Prompt pack (attached): orion_prompt_pack_v1.json
- Proposed eval spec (attached): orion-eval-spec-48hr.md

If that plan sounds good, I’ll ask Ben + Karthik to provision the eval pool and Marissa to schedule a short kickoff to validate security/ingress.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Lee <jamie@orioncommerce.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 12:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Orion Commerce — Post-demo shortlist and ops asks

Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: our SLAs are stricter in checkout — we need P95 end-to-end < 120ms for 512-token runs. If RW-13B lands around 95ms/token as you noted, that looks promising, but can you clarify whether those numbers include our typical pre/post-processing?
2) Quality: highest priority for product descriptions is precision — we want fewer hallucinated specs even if fluency drops slightly.
3) Security: can you confirm we can run the 48-hour eval in a private VPC or otherwise ensure PII never leaves our environment? We'll need a short security attestation before we proceed.

If those boxes are checked, we can greenlight the 48h eval next Tue. Also please send a ballpark cost estimate for running RW-13B in production for a 1M-token monthly workload so our finance folks can eyeball it.

—Jamie
Jamie Lee
Head of Platform, Orion Commerce
jamie@orioncommerce.com

Thanks Jamie — quick answers and proposed execution plan below.

Security / infra
- We can run the 48-hour eval inside a dedicated private VPC host for Orion (no PII egress). Karthik, can you confirm the VPC image + private registry details? (cc'd).

Latency numbers note
- Our published median/95th metrics are server-side inference only. End-to-end with your preprocess/postprocess typically adds ~30-40ms depending on your pipeline. We will instrument a small synthetic run to measure true P95 for your stack during the first 4 hours of the eval.

Cost estimate (very rough ballpark for 1M tokens / month)
- RW-2.7B-optim: ~$120/month equivalent
- RW-13B-quant: ~$410/month equivalent
- RW-70B-quant: ~$1,950/month equivalent
(These are illustrative — final pricing depends on sustained concurrency and batching profiles; Ben will produce a more formal estimate for finance.)

Proposed next steps (action owners)
- Karthik: provision the private eval VPC and pre-load orion_prompt_pack_v1.json; share ingress details by Tue 8/3 10:00 PT.
- Ben: generate the cost model and an output sample with postproc included (deliverable: orion_latency_benchmarks_aug2027.csv). Target first draft by Wed 8/4.
- Marissa: coordinate the kickoff call with Orion security to sign the short attestation and unblock the VPC run (target Tue 8/3 EOD).
- Naomi: run the two-day eval and provide initial dashboards + a 10-sample human eval set by Thu EOD.

If everyone is aligned I’ll schedule the short kickoff and lock the 48h window.

Best,
Naomi
